names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 21 iunie, «Sfântul Mucenic Iulian din Tars».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Ιουλιανός από την Κιλικία», with the rank word and the country left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 21. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученик Јулијан Тарсанин“ — Свети is not a rank and мученик is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off, and Тарсанин is **kept**, being the by-name the heading itself gives. **Keeping it is the whole reason this folder does not fold, and the saving is measured**: `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Јулијан Тарсанин», and for the bare «Јулијан» it returns four holders — `julian-companion-of-pamphilus`, `julian-of-antinoopolis`, `julian-of-samosata` and `julian-presbyter-of-ancyra`, all `sr` — which this folder would have made a fifth. This is the 18 June rule paying for itself a second time, and more dearly: there it kept two of one day’s own folders apart, here it keeps one folder out of a fold of five. The folder’s Romanian form «Iulian din Tars» carries the same by-name in its own language, so two calendars agree that the city belongs to his name.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 16 марта ст. ст., «Иулиан Аназарвский, мч.», with the rank word left off. The Russian by-name is the city of his birth, where the Romanian, Greek and Serbian forms this folder holds all name Tarsus, the city his mother moved to.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 16 марта ст. ст. — «Мч. Иулиана Аназарвского (IV).»

attestations.note: This is an identification, and here is the whole of what it rests on. The Russian calendar keeps this man on 16 марта where the Romanian, Greek and Serbian keep him on 21 June, so the match is not on the day but on the dossier, and the Russian life page gives three things that the doxologia life this folder was built from gives as well: the city of Anazarbus, which is in his Russian by-name; that his relics were at Antioch; and that John Chrysostom honoured him with a word of praise, which this page makes his 47th homily. Three coincidences and no fourth man: the Russian calendar's own 21 июня ст. ст. page was fetched and read and names no Иулиан at all, so this calendar keeps him once, here. Two things do differ and are recorded rather than smoothed: this page puts the suffering itself at Antioch in Syria and under Maximian Galerius, 305 to 311, where doxologia has him carried through the cities of Cilicia under Diocletian and killed at Aegae; and the page disagrees with itself on the rank, heading the life «Священномученик Иулиан Аназаврский» while the day's own line reads «Мч.». No date was written: this folder deliberately records none, because the one year doxologia prints is the year of a burial, and the Russian reign is kept in this note instead. The day page prints no hymn under his name. If the author reads these as two men, the row comes off and a second folder is the answer.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 21 iunie — «Sfântul Mucenic Iulian din Tars»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Ιουλιανός από την Κιλικία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. It is plainly the same man, and against nine other Julians in the corpus the details settle it: a pagan senator father and a Christian mother who brought him up by the Gospel, a confession before the eparch Marcian at eighteen, the mother sent to talk him out of it and telling him instead to stand fast, and death in a sack of poisonous snakes thrown into the deepest part of the sea. saint.gr calls his city Diocaesarea of Cilicia where doxologia.ro's life has Anazarbus with his mother afterwards at Tarsus; both are in Cilicia, the difference is the sources', and no `dates` are proposed because saint.gr gives no year. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.07.2026 (21. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Јулијан Тарсанин“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 21 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A YEAR IS PRINTED AND THE YEAR IS REFUSED, BECAUSE IT IS THE YEAR OF A BURIAL.** This folder holds `dates: null`, both its books having printed no year and both saying so in the folder’s own prose — doxologia names Diocletian and the governor Marcian and no year, saint.gr names the eparch Marcian and no year. This book prints one number: „Мошти његове избаце таласи на обалу, и верни пренесу их у Александрију и чесно сахране 290. године“ — the waves cast his relics ashore, and the faithful carried them to Alexandria and buried them honourably **in the year 290**. That is the year of the burial of the relics at Alexandria. It is not stated of the death, the book names no interval between the two, and **the corpus has no field for a burial**, so putting 290 into `death` would be putting one event’s year into another event’s field — the same class of move as a lifespan or a year got by arithmetic, and refused for the same reason. `dates` stays null. The year is recorded here, as the thing it is. **It is the author’s to overturn**: if a burial’s year is judged close enough to a martyrdom’s, this folder takes `death` 290 to 290, display «290», basis traditional, and the sentence above is its note. Note that 290 sits inside Diocletian, whom both other books name — which is not a reason to write it, a reign being no source for a year, and is only the reason the refused year is not absurd. **AND THE YEAR IS KEPT OUT OF THE PROSE ON PURPOSE.** This folder lacks `death`, so `date-audit` reads its life for a year, and a refused year sitting in a paragraph beside a death verb is how `stated` moves. The paragraph written today therefore **carries no four-digit number at all**, which is the safest shape the standing rule names, and the number lives here instead. WHAT IS NEW, AND THE TWO QUOTATIONS ARE THE BEST OF IT. The folder already records that John Chrysostom praised him, off doxologia’s one clause. **This book quotes him, twice, and neither quotation is in either other book**: „Из уста мученика исходио је свети глас, и заједно с гласом изливала се светлост јаснија од сунчаних зрака“ — out of the martyr’s mouth came a holy voice, and with the voice poured out a light clearer than the rays of the sun; and „Узми кога било, сумашедшег и бесног, и приведи овоме светоме гробу, где су мошти мученикове, и видећеш, како ће он (демон) непремено искочити и побећи као од палећег жара“ — take anyone you like, out of his wits and raving, and bring him to this holy tomb where the martyr’s relics are, and you will see how he will certainly leap out and flee as from a burning coal. `john-chrysostom` is `related` on this folder already and its life already names him, so the row is not touched and the name may stand in the prose as it already does. THE SACK, AND A THIRD THING IN IT. doxologia had sand and venomous beasts and creeping things; saint.gr had poisonous snakes. This book has „врећу с песком и са скорпијама и змијама“ — sand, **scorpions** and snakes, the scorpions being new. THE MOTHER, WHO DIES HERE UNDER THE TORMENTS AND IS NAMED BY NOBODY. „а и мајка Јулијанова умре на мукама“. doxologia had her heels cut off and her driven away and called her end a martyr’s too; this book has her die in the torments themselves, which is a plainer end than either other book gives. **She takes no row and no folder**: a narrated martyrdom with no name gets neither, and not one of the three books names her. The „три дана“ she spent in the prison counselling him the opposite of what she was sent to counsel agree with doxologia exactly. The governor is only „намесник царски“ here, where the other two books name him Marcian; no row, and the name is not imported into this book’s account. `types` UNTOUCHED. Свети is not a rank, мученик is the rank and gives the `martyr` the folder carries, and the heading has nothing else. „Благородног, сенаторског порекла“ — of noble, senatorial descent — stands in the body, is said of him where doxologia said it of his father, and is no type in this corpus. No `office`, no `locations`: Tarsus, Aegae, Alexandria and Antioch are named in clauses. **No rows** beyond the one that exists. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED, AND ON THIS DAY THAT COSTS SOMETHING. The ПЕСМА for 21 June is the longest of the wave so far and it tells a scene the prose entry does not: Julian building a tomb for his brother Julius beside their ninety-ninth church, Julius telling him mildly to prepare himself, for the grave is built for him and he will go before his brother, and God appointing Julius to build the hundredth church on a lonely island. **It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account**, and §3 of this wave’s brief puts the verse in no field and in no life; so the scene is recorded here, where a reading belongs, and written into neither paragraph. THE DAY’S THIRD ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE CORPUS HAS ALREADY REFUSED THIS MAN ONCE. „Свети мученик Арчил II, цар грузињски“ — Archil II, king of Georgia, son of king Stephen and grandson of the great Georgian king Vakhtang, a great Christian and a protector of Christianity, tortured by the Muslims and beheaded for Christ on 20 March 744, being eighty years old when he suffered. `ls saints | grep -iE 'archil|luarsab'` returns nobody and `grep -ril Archil saints/*/saint.json` returns exactly one folder: `six-thousand-martyrs-of-david-gareji`, whose own attestation note already says that «the **king Archil of Georgia** gathered all the martyrs’ relics and buried them honourably» and that **«Arsenius and Archil are named as the entry names them and identified with nobody»**. So this is not a reader’s first refusal of Archil but the corpus’s second, and the two agree: he is named and he gets no folder. Ruling 3, therefore — and **20 March 744, the eighty years and the lineage are written nowhere**, the eighty years being a lifespan besides. `vakhtang-gorgasali` exists and takes no row and no mention in any prose written today: a grandfather is a kinship, but there is no grandson’s folder for it to be a kinship on. THE DAY’S FOURTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети мученик Луарсаб II, књаз карталински у Грузији“ — Luarsab II, prince of Kartli in Georgia, whose father George X also suffered for the faith and was poisoned by the Persian shah; thrown into a prison near Shiraz where he lay seven years, and then by the order of shah Abbas I hanged in the prison together with two servants, on 21 June 1622, with a heavenly light seen over his grave. `ls saints | grep -i luarsab` returns nobody, and `grep -ril Luarsab saints/*/saint.json` returns nobody either; `grep -ril Kartli` holds four Georgian folders and none of them is he. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written today, no folder from me, and **1622, the seven years, George X, Abbas I and the two servants are written nowhere**. The two servants are a narrated martyrdom with no name, which takes no row and no folder on the settled rule.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Iulian, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Iulian din Tars, glasul 4; the text is the common of a single martyr, printed with his name in it.

english.text: Thy martyr Julian, O Lord, in his contest received the crown of incorruption from Thee our God; for having Thy strength he overcame the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Μητρικαὶς ὑποθήκαις μυσταγωγούμενος, πανευκλεὴς στρατιώτης ὤφθης Χριστοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, παντευχίαν μυστικὴν περιζωσάμενος• ὅθεν καθεῖλες τὸν ἔχθρον, ὡς γενναῖος ἀριστεύς, καὶ ἤθλησας θεοφρόνως, Ἰουλιανὲ θεόφρον, ὑπὲρ ἠμῶν ἀεὶ πρεσβεύων Θεῶ.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the only apolytikion on the page of «Άγιος Ιουλιανός από την Κιλικία», and it names him and his mother's counsels

english.text: Initiated by a mother's counsels, you were shown an all-glorious soldier of Christ our God, having girded on the whole mystical armour; whence you brought down the enemy like a noble champion and contended with a godly mind, O God-minded Julian, ever interceding with God for us.
